source.display_title: 05/12/2026 - Steven Silbert x Farooq Bey  — Follow Up

call.sequence_note: The rep opens by referencing a previous conversation and elects to reset — 'It's been probably like 15 calls since I last spoke to you. So I don't want to operate under previous assumptions. So let's kind of treat this like a fresh call.' He also refers back to it later ('how I, I think I said this the other day'). The earlier call is not identifiable within this batch.

prospect.name: Cole Carson
prospect.location: Not stated; works out of an office at his church. Recently moved house.
prospect.occupation: Youth ministry at a church, working with high school and middle school students
prospect.family_status: Married; one young daughter. Household rule that any purchase over $100 is discussed jointly.
prospect.training_background: Was around 220 lb before his wedding and lost weight, which became part of his identity for a period — jump rope, kettlebells, clean eating, fitness podcasts. Now streaky: 'I'll have a week where I'll get three or four workouts in, the next week is crazy so I don't get it in.' Stays generally non-sedentary with an e-bike commute, a walking treadmill at a standing desk, and picking up a kettlebell at random through the day. Self-directed by habit and admits pride in it. Rates himself six or seven out of ten for longevity readiness.

signals: Explicitly good-to-great and not rescue — 'if I get absolutely shredded, amazing, but I'm really looking for the longevity aspects' and 'I feel like where I'm at, I can maintain for a long time, but I want to go past that'
Health-literate and already active: e-bike commute, walking treadmill, organic and clean eating with his wife, ad-hoc kettlebell work

Diverges sharply from the optimizer on price, which is why confidence is only 0.6: roughly $4-5K liquid, a single credit card with about the same available, a recent house move, and a household rule requiring a joint conversation on anything over $100. He declined $9,000, $6,000 and $4,000 and deferred on $200/month.

Also carries a self-directed streak the optimizer definition does not capture — 'I've always been a guy that's like, I'm doing my own workouts, I'm doing my own kettlebell thing... so maybe a little bit of pride in there, like, oh, I don't need help'

goals.text: Move well for a very long time — 'I want to be able to move really well for a long time' rather than get shredded
A sustainable programme he can actually stay consistent with, ending the streaky on-off cycle
Address tight hips before they become a problem
Be physically able to say yes to his daughter and future grandchildren — 'if my daughter's like, hey, I want to go backpacking for a week... I don't want to miss out on the memories'
Not be the grandfather stuck with a walker who cannot play catch
Show up better for his wife — better mood, less stress, more present — and inspire her to start lifting
Live the example for the middle and high school students in his ministry
Get intentionally stronger rather than just staying non-sedentary

pains.text: Streaky, inconsistent training — three or four workouts one week, none the next, back and forth
Since having a child, the pockets of time that exist are not when he wants to train — 'it's not what I want to go do at that moment because I finally have a moment to myself'
Tight hips, which he names as the main thing needing attention before it becomes a problem
Moving but not moving intentionally — 'the moving part, I do pretty well, but like being intentionally mobile and like intentionally getting stronger, I haven't been hitting that'
Has become comfortable with deprioritising himself — 'it's kind of become the norm for me, you know, just making sure I get all the other stuff done'
Pride in self-sufficiency has kept him from getting help — 'maybe a little bit of pride in there, like, oh, I don't need help'
Has the knowledge but cannot assemble it — 'I feel like I have all this stuff. I just need help putting it together'
Tight finances after a recent house move with a young child — around $4-5K liquid and a $100 household discussion threshold

objections.raw_quote: Well, I mean, to be honest with you, that's quite a bit for me and for my family. So definitely something that I'm going to have to think about. can't just just Pull that trigger by myself without talking to my wife and stuff, but yeah, wherever we're at, we just moved and stuff. So that sounds like it's going to be a bit much for me to handle right now.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play properly — isolated first ('to put the investment aside for a second, Cole, do you want to do this?'), asked why he wanted it, framed with 'the last thing I want to do is take food off your table', then asked permission for a financial conversation and worked through cash on hand, credit cards, available credit and credit score

objections.raw_quote: Yeah. I consider it right now that it is like quite a bit, you know, we basically couldn't, I couldn't do it right now, if I'm being completely honest, so.
objections.rep_response: Read the numbers honestly and declined to take the money — 'the last thing I want for you to do is just, you know, to take up your cash on hand, your credit card amount and just say, come in for the 9k, or even the 6' — then improvised a $4,000 three-month tier at roughly $400/month over twelve months

objections.raw_quote: Um, you know, to be honest, I don't, I don't think so, man. If I'm being completely honest, I just, I know where we're at right now and the conversations that me and my wife are having, it's just a little bit out there.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and moved to the $200/month Primal University downsell with a screen share, framed as a one-month extraction

objections.raw_quote: My wife and I, usually, we have a rule that we talk about things that are, like, over $100 purchase, so I'm not just going for it without talking to you... because diapers and blah, blah, you know.
objections.rep_response: Did not run the partner play at all — no name asked, no receptiveness check, no permission-versus-FYI question, no invitation to join, no deposit fallback. Booked a 10-minute follow-up for Thursday instead.

offer.payment_plan_terms: In-house plan floated for the main tiers. For the improvised three-month tier: $4,000 spread over 12 months at roughly $400/month, which totals about $4,800. Primal University offered at $200/month, cancellable at any time.

prospect_financials.credit_score: self-reported as high, exact figure unknown to him

evidence: Declined all coaching tiers. On $6,000 and $9,000: 'that's quite a bit for me and for my family'. On the $4,000 three-month at $400/month: 'to be honest, I don't, I don't think so, man.'
Deferred rather than declined on the $200/month Primal University: 'I'll definitely think on it, but that sounds pretty awesome'
A concrete next step was booked — a 10-minute call the following Thursday, with a calendar invite sent and the prospect asked to confirm it
Blocker is genuine and disclosed in detail: roughly $4-5K liquid, one credit card with about $4-5K available, a recent house move, and a household rule to discuss anything over $100 jointly
Counter-evidence on intent: strong desire throughout — 'it sounds like exactly what I need' and, asked whether he wanted to do it, 'Yeah, I mean, I would love to do it'
No payment link sent and no money collected, so the close rule does not apply
outcome.next_step: 10-minute follow-up call on Thursday after he speaks to his wife, primarily about the $200/month Primal University option.

notable.note: Second mis-titled file in this batch. The title names Steven Silbert; the call is entirely with Cole Carson, a 32-year-old youth minister. Taken with the 05/11 file titled Shawn Panjwani that actually contains Steven Silbert's call, titles in this rep's folder cannot be trusted for prospect identity. This is also, on process, the best money play in the batch: the rep isolated, asked permission, worked the full cash-on-hand, credit-card and credit-score sequence, and then read the numbers honestly and declined to take the money — 'the last thing I want for you to do is just take up your cash on hand, your credit card amount and just say, come in for the 9k, or even the 6.' He then undercut that by improvising an unsanctioned $4,000 three-month tier financed at about $400/month. He also advised buying Primal University for one month specifically to extract and cancel: 'come in for a month, extract everything you need, get your notepad and pen, write what you need to write, and then just cancel it.' No medical conditions were disclosed on this call.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion. The rep's questions repeatedly sit under the prospect's label — 'Why a six or seven?', 'Just roughly', 'And what's the available amount, again, roughly?' — while long prospect answers about mobility and his hips appear under the rep's. One passage around 00:02:00 runs the prospect's entire answer inside a rep-labelled block. Roles resolved from content. The rep misstates the tiers once as 'Four months and six' before correctly giving six and twelve.
